newsitem.title: USA: United Meridian oil, gas production rising.
newsitem.headline: United Meridian oil, gas production rising.

text.p: United Meridian Corp expects to boost oil and natural gas production from both its domestic and international operations this year, Chairman John Brock said on Tuesday.

The company expects average crude oil production to rise to about 20,000 to 25,000 barrels per day (bpd) this year from 16,000 bpd produced in 1996, in large part due to increased production from its stake in an offshore Equitorial Guinea field, he said.

Natural gas production should rise to about 150 million to 160 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) in 1997 from last year's 145 mmcfd on increased production from its core North American fields, he said.
"We're going to grow, both in North America and international," Brock said at the annual Howard Weil energy conference here.

United Meridian will take a 22 percent share of the 70,000 to 75,000 bpd production expected to come on line this summer at Block B Phase II of the Equitorial Guinea offshore tract operated by Mobil Corp, he said. Current production from the wells there was pegged at 50,000 bpd, he said.
Worldwide, the company plans to participate in drilling 225 development wells and 75 exploration wells this year.

United Meridian has built up a $325 million warchest in cash and a credit facility, and is eyeing potential acquisitions of either a rival exploration and development company or drilling properties, he said.
But after paring down operating costs and expanding its international portfolio in recent years, the company is being cautious about any acquisitions.
"We're going to be very careful on how we pull the trigger," he said.
